about.title: Larkspur Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Larkspur's mix of small retail centers, marina-adjacent businesses, and commercial spots along Magnolia Avenue and Sir Francis Drake Boulevard means workplace injuries here range from delivery accidents near US-101 to falls at job sites and equipment mishaps in local shops and offices. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, property owner, delivery vehicle driver, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured Larkspur workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to your situation, explain your options in plain terms, and help you understand deadlines before they pass. There's no obligation to move forward, and no cost to start the conversation.

whyChoose.title: Why Larkspur Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Your Exclusive Remedy Limits
items.desc: California generally treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but that doesn't cover every angle. An independent attorney can help identify if a third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — bears separate responsibility.

items.title: Protecting Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation for reporting a workplace injury. If you're worried about your job while recovering, an attorney can explain your protections and help you report within the required 30-day window.

items.title: Watching the Two-Year Clock on Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Unlike workers' comp, a third-party injury claim in California generally must be filed within two years. Missing that deadline can close off compensation options entirely, so early guidance matters.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near US-101 in Larkspur — is that a workers' comp claim or something else?
items.answer: It depends on who caused the injury. If it was purely a workplace accident, workers' comp is typically your path regardless of fault. But if another company's driver, a subcontractor, or defective equipment played a role, a separate third-party claim against that party may also be available — an independent attorney can help sort out which applies.

items.question: Do I have to report my injury to my employer right away?
items.answer: Yes — California generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Reporting late can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it's best to notify your employer as soon as you're able after the incident.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Larkspur?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can walk you through your options.
